name: Six-Axis Robot

speed.label: Joint speed (°/s)
speed.desc: Top speed along the joint-space path. All six joints are driven from one path parameter, so they start and arrive together instead of the fastest one finishing early.

accel.label: Joint accel (°/s²)
accel.desc: How hard the arm ramps to and from the joint speed. Lower it for a heavier or more delicate payload; a short move may never reach top speed at all.

scale.label: Scale
scale.desc: Uniform size multiplier on the whole robot, applied to its collision bodies as well as its appearance - so a scaled arm really does reach further, rather than just looking bigger.

toolSizeX.label: Tool size X (m)
toolSizeX.desc: Length of the vacuum plate. The orange dots on the tool itself drag this in the viewport, and they ride the arm, so you can size the tool in whatever pose you are inspecting. Size it to the product you are picking - the plate is also the grab reach.

toolSizeZ.label: Tool size Z (m)
toolSizeZ.desc: Width of the vacuum plate, dragged by the same orange dots on the tool.

cupPitchX.label: Cup pitch X (m)
cupPitchX.desc: Centre-to-centre spacing of the suction cups along the plate length. The plate fits as many as the pitch allows, so tightening it adds cups rather than moving them.

cupPitchZ.label: Cup pitch Z (m)
cupPitchZ.desc: Centre-to-centre spacing of the suction cups across the plate width.

cupMarginX.label: Cup margin X (m)
cupMarginX.desc: Inset from each end of the plate before the first cup, so the grid does not run off the edge.

cupMarginZ.label: Cup margin Z (m)
cupMarginZ.desc: Inset from each side of the plate before the first cup.

cupsEnabled.label: Suction cups
cupsEnabled.desc: Draw the cup grid under the plate. Appearance only - the grip itself comes from the vacuum tag, not from the cups being visible.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Connect this robot to a PLC program. Its tags appear once this is on. Without a program the arm rests at its idle pose.

commandTag.label: Command tag (job number)
commandTag.desc: Which job to run: 1 is the first job, 2 the second and so on. Set it BEFORE pulsing execute. A robot with no jobs takes a waypoint row here instead (0 is home). A number with no job or row behind it is ignored, and the arm stays put rather than guessing.

executeTag.label: Execute tag (rising edge runs it)
executeTag.desc: Pulse this false-to-true to start the job. It is edge-triggered, so holding it true does NOT repeat - drop it and raise it again for each job.

doneTag.label: Done tag (true while idle)
doneTag.desc: Handshake back to the program: true whenever the robot is ready for the next command. A job that ends on a Blend move reports done as it rounds that corner, so the next job can carry straight on. Wait for it before pulsing execute again, or the edge lands mid-job and is dropped.

enableTag.label: Enable tag
enableTag.desc: The robot moves only while this is true. Drop it and the arm brakes to a stop where it is and the job holds, timers and all; raise it and the job carries on. Wire it to the cell being safe to work in. Leave it empty and the robot is always enabled.

gripperTag.label: Vacuum tag
gripperTag.desc: For a robot with no jobs: grip or release the load, read continuously, so hold it true for the whole carry. A robot with jobs switches its own vacuum with Vacuum steps and ignores this.

in1Tag.label: Input 1 tag
in1Tag.desc: A signal a job can wait on (a Wait for step). Robots have banks of these; wire the ones your jobs use.

in2Tag.label: Input 2 tag
in2Tag.desc: A signal a job can wait on (a Wait for step).

in3Tag.label: Input 3 tag
in3Tag.desc: A signal a job can wait on (a Wait for step).

in4Tag.label: Input 4 tag
in4Tag.desc: A signal a job can wait on (a Wait for step).

out1Tag.label: Output 1 tag
out1Tag.desc: A signal a job switches (a Set step), to tell the program where it has got to. It holds its last value between jobs.

out2Tag.label: Output 2 tag
out2Tag.desc: A signal a job switches (a Set step).

out3Tag.label: Output 3 tag
out3Tag.desc: A signal a job switches (a Set step).

out4Tag.label: Output 4 tag
out4Tag.desc: A signal a job switches (a Set step).

waypoints.label: Waypoints
waypoints.desc: The poses this robot knows, one row of six JOINT angles each - not a position in space, so the arm reaches a pose exactly as taught with no ambiguity about elbow or wrist. Name them, and jobs move to them by name. Pose the arm with the viewport gizmo and use Capture Pose to add one rather than typing angles.

blendWaypoints.label: Pass-through waypoints (robots without jobs)
blendWaypoints.desc: For a robot with no jobs: which waypoints are VIA points. The arm reports done before it reaches one, so the next move can start while it is still running and the corner is rounded instead of braked to a stop. Jobs say this on each Move step instead.

blendDeg.label: Corner blend
blendDeg.desc: How many joint degrees before a via point the arm starts cutting the corner. Larger rounds the path more and strays further from the taught pose; the arm caps it at a third of the move.

ops.label: Move
ops.desc: Move the arm to a waypoint. Stop arrives exactly and stands still; Blend rounds the corner and carries on into the next move, for poses that are only on the way somewhere.

ops.label: Vacuum
ops.desc: Switch the tool vacuum. The load is held from the step it goes on to the step it goes off.

ops.label: Wait
ops.desc: Stand still for a time, to let a grip seal or a load settle. The clock stops while the robot is not enabled.

ops.label: Wait for
ops.desc: Hold here until one of the robot inputs reads on (or off). This is how a job waits on the cell: a pallet in place, a zone clear.

ops.label: Set
ops.desc: Switch one of the robot outputs, to tell the PLC something the job has reached: clear of the table, load released.

jobs.label: Jobs
jobs.desc: The robot's own programs. The PLC runs one by number (the command tag) and the robot does the whole thing: moves, vacuum, waits, and the signals it sends back. While the scene runs, the step being run is highlighted.

pose.label: Idle pose
pose.desc: The pose a freshly placed robot rests in, and where one waiting for its first Execute sits. It is the arm you see in a stopped scene, so set it to something that reads as parked rather than mid-cycle.
